original.reason: The proposed primitive-root ordering does not establish the claim. For p>3, a primitive root g modulo p has g^2 not congruent to 1 modulo p, so v_p(g^2-1)=0, not 1; the displayed geometric sum then has valuation n, not n-1. Also primitiveness modulo p^n alone does not imply g^N is nontrivial modulo p^{n+1}. Thus the proof fails, though it addresses the stated problem.

judgment.reason: It falsely claims that primitiveness modulo p^2 makes g^2-1 divisible by p. For p>3 a primitive root modulo p is not ±1, so g^2-1 is a p-adic unit. The valuation conclusion is therefore false.
The assertion g^2≡1 modulo p is false in general for a primitive root when p>3. Hence v_p(g^2-1)=1 does not follow, and the claimed valuation of the cyclic sum fails.
From g being primitive modulo p^2 one may conclude g^2 is not 1 modulo p^2, but not that g^2-1 has valuation 1. For p>3 it has valuation 0, invalidating the result.
It incorrectly infers v_p(g^2-1)=1 from primitiveness modulo p^2. This fails for every p>3, so the constructed ordering does not prove the required nondivisibility.
